principle: ASI rubric governs how Human, AI, Wisdom and other domain registries may interact across multiple Sequences. It does not replace those rubrics and it does not rewrite source truth.

segments.name: Identity / Scope Governance
segments.purpose: Govern followed object, identity continuity, resolution, inclusion/exclusion and closure scope.

segments.name: Truth / Provenance Governance
segments.purpose: Enforce source custody, provenance, proof depth, evidence separation and epistemic labeling.

segments.name: Sequence / Closure Governance
segments.purpose: Enforce R-F-R, barrier law, no reopen, terminal contracts, closure packets and scope-correct closure.

segments.name: Cross-Sequence Coordination
segments.purpose: Coordinate Main, Rider, Attached, Counter, Parallel, Converging, Next, Reference and Observer Sequences.

segments.name: Cross-Domain Synthesis
segments.purpose: Combine Human, AI, Wisdom and other domain activations while retaining ownership, source and contradiction boundaries.

segments.name: Wisdom / Value / Principle Governance
segments.purpose: Use contextual wisdom and value priorities without converting interpretation into source fact or bypassing current reality.

segments.name: Rule / Priority / Exception Governance
segments.purpose: Resolve rule conflicts, priorities, promises, overrides and exception contracts with explicit authority and consequence.

segments.name: Safety / Permission / Authority
segments.purpose: Govern permissions, prohibitions, access, authority, intervention boundaries and accountability.

segments.name: Contradiction Governance
segments.purpose: Preserve unresolved conflicts, route investigation and prevent silent consensus fabrication.

segments.name: Uncertainty / Unknown Governance
segments.purpose: Keep unknown, unavailable, contradictory, not-applicable and speculative states machine-visible.

segments.name: Memory Governance
segments.purpose: Govern storage class, source binding, overwrite policy, versioning, trust, retrieval and contamination controls.

segments.name: Learning / Evolution Governance
segments.purpose: Govern what can change, where it may write, which version is affected and which learning mechanism is permitted.

segments.name: Resource Governance
segments.purpose: Coordinate compute, storage, concurrency, tools, external actors and shared resource conflicts.

segments.name: Version / Migration / Rollback
segments.purpose: Preserve historical states, canonical precedence, migration rules and reversible system updates.

segments.name: Long-Horizon / Future Consequence
segments.purpose: Track latent effects, downstream criticality, seeds, systemic consequences and future convergence windows.

segments.name: Multi-Agent / Multi-Human Coordination
segments.purpose: Coordinate multiple humans, artificial agents, institutions and distributed controllers without collapsing Actor Views.

segments.name: Law / Principle Formation
segments.purpose: Convert supported closed-case patterns into candidate guidance, rules or laws with exceptions and provenance.

segments.name: Meta-Reasoning / Self-Audit
segments.purpose: Audit reasoning paths, mechanism choice, proof debt, graph gaps, controller assumptions and internal contradictions.

segments.name: Goal Conflict / Arbitration
segments.purpose: Resolve competing ends, priorities, duties, wants, needs and long-horizon consequences under declared authority.

segments.name: Global Closure / Era Transition
segments.purpose: Distinguish local closure from higher-scope project, institution, war, civilization or era transition and determine what seeds the next reality.

hard_guards: ASI rubric cannot overwrite Human, AI or Wisdom native registry definitions.
ASI governance cannot convert a local closure into global closure without closure-scope evidence.
ASI governance cannot give an actor knowledge absent from that actor's View Map.
ASI governance cannot bypass Barrier Law or accept a required return that failed its acceptance condition.
ASI governance cannot manufacture provenance or silently merge contradiction.
